transcript:
--- Meeting Header ---
Date: 2025-09-02 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Lina Rodriguez (Valerian Head of ML), Tom Ellis (Eng Manager), Priya Shah (SRE), Samir Gupta (CTO joined 00:12:30)

Summary: quick intro to Redwood hosted chat (serverless flavors), live console tour of streaming params, retry/backoff patterns, and where Optimize suggests batching/quantization for cost. Discussed security concerns (SOC2, KMS), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a pilot.

Topics: Hosted serverless mode vs dedicated pools; streaming behavior and partial payloads; retry/backoff and idempotency; console Optimize suggestions; simple perf benchmarking plan; security/Qs.

Action notes: see action_items field.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm aisha with redwood inference, im the account lead for valerian today. quick sound check?
[00:06] Lina: yep good here, lina.
[00:08] Tom: tom here, we can hear you.
[00:12] Marcus: hey team, im marcus, i'll be the SE. i'll demo console and run through a streaming example.
[00:16] Priya: priya here, i'll ask the infra and security Qs.
[00:22] Aisha: great. agenda: high-level hosted flow, console live tour, streaming params and backoff patterns, then q&a and next steps.
[00:30] Lina: sounds good, our primary goals are low-latency chat for clinical intake (under 300ms p95 if possible) and strong data residency/retention controls.
[00:40] Marcus: okay noted. two quick clarifications — when you say "low latency" is that for single-turn prompts or multi-turn with long histories?
[00:46] Lina: mostly multi-turn but we can trim history in prod — the critical thing is responsiveness during intake.
[00:54] Tom: and cost is a factor, since we're operating on a budget for inference.
[00:58] Marcus: makes sense — i'll show a few levers in the console: streaming chunk size, token limits, and automatic prefix cache which helps multi-turn.
[01:08] [01:08] Marcus: starting the console share - loading project dashboard... (screen noise)
[01:15] Marcus: here we have serverless hosted endpoint — we call it "serverless" internally, it's the fastest way to start (no reserved GPUs). it auto-scales and you pay per-token.
[01:28] Aisha: important to call out: serverless is different from dedicated pools — dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale but requires a commit.
[01:36] Lina: if we need guarantees for clinical SLAs would we need dedicated?
[01:40] Marcus: depends — if you need strict SLOs and sustained throughput, dedicated is the route. for initial pilot serverless often hits latency targets with smaller concurrency.
[01:50] [02:00] Marcus: demoing a chat request now. streaming enabled -> see stream frames arriving as tokens. sometimes the client sees partial frames and can render progressively.
[02:12] Marcus: note on transcription — sometimes the SDK prints model names oddly, e.g., "redwood-alpha" gets transcribed different in logs, small quirk.
[02:20] Tom: what's the default timeout on streaming?
[02:23] Marcus: default is 30s on the client side, but you can raise/lower per-route. also there's a keepalive ping to keep long polls open.
[02:32] Priya: what about retry semantics? if we get an internal error midway through a stream, can we resume or must we restart?
[02:39] Marcus: good Q. we expose a resumable token offset for some models — but standard pattern is idempotent retries with an idempotency key so you either re-request and de-dupe on your side, or use our prefix/K V cache to avoid recomputing.
[02:53] Lina: KV cache? how reliable is it across serverless instances?
[02:57] Marcus: it's global per-customer prefix cache — in serverless it's backed by our distributed cache, it's eventual consistent for fast reuse. we recommend prefix caching for multi-turn to reduce compute.
[03:08] [03:20] Marcus: switching to console Optimize tab — it surfaces batching suggestions and quantization profiles based on observed tokens. it will say e.g., "enable int8 for this workload" or "batch size 8 recommended" — small suggestions.
[03:35] Aisha: and Optimize also shows estimated unit cost savings and latency impact so you can trade off.
[03:42] Tom: is that automated or manual? can we auto-apply recommendations?
[03:46] Marcus: currently manual — you review and apply a profile per route. automated apply coming later this quarter but not yet GA.
[03:54] Lina: in terms of telemetry, can we get token-level breakdowns, tracing?
[03:58] Marcus: yes, console gives trace per-request, and you can export detailed token cost breakdowns. retention windows are configurable as an enterprise add-on.
[04:10] [04:30] Priya: security — where are logs stored, do you support customer-managed KMS?
[04:35] Aisha: yes, for enterprise/private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integrations; hosted has encrypted-at-rest logs, and we can arrange SOC2 artifacts.
[04:44] Priya: do you offer VPC peering or private link?
[04:47] Marcus: for private deployment we offer VPC and on-prem; for hosted serverless we do private link into certain regions — specific details we'll cover in the security deep dive.
[04:58] Samir: (joined) apologies for delay, CTO here. my main Q — does serverless store PHI anywhere? we need to ensure no persistent copies without controls.
[05:08] Marcus: good timing — serverless processes requests transiently; logs are optional and can be disabled for the route. for PHI we recommend private deployment or dedicated with customer KMS and strict retention policies.
[05:22] Samir: ok.
[05:24] [05:30] Marcus: now a quick live test: sending a prompt with a 600 token history to simulate clinical intake. watching the p50/p95 in the console metrics.
[05:40] Marcus: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 around 480ms in this sandbox region — this is best-effort and depends on sequence length.
[05:50] Tom: those p95 numbers are promising, what about tokenized cost bump with histories?
[05:55] Marcus: yes cost scales with total input+output tokens; Optimize can suggest compression strategies (summarize history, shorter system prompts) and batching only helps when you have many concurrent requests.
[06:07] Lina: can Optimize suggest paraphrase compression automatically?
[06:11] Marcus: not yet automated, but we have eval rules that flag long histories and suggestions to summarize. it's in the roadmap.
[06:18] [06:30] Tom: if a stream errors at token 120, what's the recommended pattern for the client?
[06:34] Marcus: recommended: client detect failure, attempt an idempotent retry with same idempotency key. if partial output mattered, you can resume from cache offset for compatible models, but resumption isn't universal. backoff strategy: exponential with jitter, start at 200ms, cap ~5s, 3 attempts for non-idempotent flows.
[06:55] Priya: do you provide client SDK helpers for that?
[06:58] Marcus: yes, SDK includes retry helpers and helpers to generate idempotency keys and to stitch stream frames if you persist them.
[07:08] [07:20] Marcus: i'm switching to a failure-mode demo — simulating a transient 503 and showing console fallback to a cheaper model variant.
[07:28] Marcus: you see our smart routing policy here: route by latency, then by cost. when the primary model is saturated, it can fallback to a quantized variant or a smaller model automatically.
[07:40] Lina: will fallback change response style/quality? we can't have clinical misinformation.
[07:46] Marcus: that's a risk — fallback can degrade quality. we recommend guardrails: set model fallback policies to only similar-quality variants, and route to canary for a subset first. also set alerts in Optimize for quality regressions tied to evaluation prompts.
[07:59] Samir: how do we test regressions?
[08:02] Marcus: you upload an eval set (a dozen critical prompts) and the platform runs continuous evals on new model versions — it will flag regressions and can block rollouts.
[08:14] Tom: nice. can we run an initial smoke perfbench with our data?
[08:18] Aisha: yes. action: Marcus will run the perf bench in sandbox using your prompt set.
[08:22] [08:30] Marcus: quick Q on SSO - do you use SAML or OIDC?
[08:33] Tom: we use SAML across the org.
[08:36] Marcus: good — we support SAML SSO and RBAC in the console.
[08:40] Priya: there's a compliance question — SOC2 + ISO attestation?
[08:43] Aisha: we have SOC2 Type II for Redwood Dedicated and hosted tiers; private deployments have additional controls and we can provide evidence.
[08:53] [09:00] Lina: what's typical pilot length companies run?
[09:04] Aisha: 4-8 weeks for a production pilot: initial integration, perf/quality evals, then a small canary.
[09:11] Lina: ok that works.
[09:14] [09:20] Marcus: back to retries: another pattern is the optimistic partial-render in the UI — show tokens as they arrive, but mark the response as "incomplete" until the final status. if a retry occurs, stitch or replace the UI block.
[09:34] Tom: any gotchas with idempotency keys collisions?
[09:37] Marcus: collisions are rare if you generate keys with UUID+timestamp+route; we also provide server-side dedupe window which you can configure.
[09:46] Priya: about data residency - can we pin region?
[09:49] Marcus: yes, routes can be region pinned; private deployments give full control. hosted serverless has regional endpoints.
[09:57] [10:10] Marcus: i'm demonstrating console's retry logs — you can see request traces and the exact retry attempts, status codes, and whether fallback applied.
[10:22] Lina: in that log i see model names spelled differently e.g., "redwoo-dp" — is that just obfuscation?
[10:28] Marcus: sometimes auto transcription or short names get truncated in the UI; we'll send a glossary to avoid confusion.
[10:36] Samir: any encryption-in-transit details?
[10:38] Aisha: all traffic TLS 1.2/1.3, support for mTLS for private link.
[10:44] [10:50] Tom: let's talk cost for a second — ballpark tokens per patient interaction? average 600 tokens input + 200 output = 800 tokens. for 10k interactions a month that's 8M tokens.
[11:03] Marcus: right, and Optimize will estimate monthly spend and show binning by model variant. we can run projections during the perf test.
[11:10] Lina: can we cap spend?
[11:12] Aisha: yes quotas per-api-key and alerts; also route-based quotas.
[11:18] [11:30] Priya: on long-term, if we went dedicated what are typical commit sizes?
[11:34] Marcus: depends on throughput — typical customer commits range from monthly $50k-$200k for mid-size usage; smaller pilots start hosted.
[11:45] Samir: that's reasonable.
[11:47] [12:00] Marcus: demo wrap up — key levers: enable prefix cache, tune streaming chunk size, use idempotency keys + SDK retry helpers, and use Optimize to identify batching/quantization.
[12:12] Tom: can you email the exact console paths and screenshots?
[12:15] Aisha: yes will share deck + recording.
[12:18] Lina: one more question — latency SLOs: is there an SLA for serverless?
[12:22] Marcus: we have SLO guidance for serverless but formal SLA available on Dedicated. we'll include that in the doc pack.
[12:30] [12:40] Priya: for the security deep dive what do you need from us?
[12:43] Aisha: list of compliance controls you require, KMS key types, and region constraints. we'll schedule the session with our security team.
[12:55] Samir: fine.
[13:00] [13:10] Marcus: final quick note — when you do retries avoid blind synchronous retries at high QPS; use backoff + circuit breaker at client.
[13:20] Lina: makes sense.
[13:25] Aisha: ok we should recap.
[13:28] [13:30] Recap:
- Redwood will share pricing + concurrency appendix (Aisha)
- Marcus will run perf tests in sandbox with Valerian prompt set and share p50/p95 and token cost estimates
- Priya to share VPC/KMS constraints
- Schedule a security deep dive w/ Redwood security (week of 2025-09-15)
- Lina to assemble a small eval prompt set for continuous quality checks

[13:55] Aisha: thanks everyone for the time, we'll follow up with notes and the sandbox plan.
[14:00] Tom: thanks.
[14:02] Lina: thanks all.
[14:05] Samir: bye.

--- End transcript ---
